history.dynasty: Pallava; Chola (present masonry structure, 9th century); Vijayanagara (later expansions)
history.period: Present masonry structure 9th century CE; site and legend older
history.summary: Ekambareswarar Temple in Kanchipuram is one of the Pancha Bhoota Sthalas - the Prithvi (earth) manifestation of Shiva - and a Paadal Petra Sthalam revered in the 7th-century Tevaram. The complex spans 25 acres (10 hectares), among India's largest temple complexes, with four gopurams, the tallest southern tower rising 11 stories (~58.5 m / 192 ft), and a thousand-pillared hall built in the Vijayanagara period. Legend holds that Goddess Kamakshi (Parvati) worshipped a sand Shiva Lingam under a mango tree here - the temple's name means 'Lord of the Mango Tree' - and married Shiva on this spot. A centuries-old mango tree in the courtyard is said to bear fruits of four tastes from four branches (the four Vedas). Six daily rituals run from early morning to 10 pm; the temple is administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE Department.

name: Ekambareswarar Temple
town_description: Kanchipuram, about 72 km southwest of Chennai, is one of Hinduism's seven holiest cities (Sapta Puri) and the 'City of a Thousand Temples', famed for Shiva and Vishnu temples and its silk sarees.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaivism; Pancha Bhoota Sthalam - Prithvi; Paadal Petra Sthalam)

travel.airport: Chennai International Airport, about 75 km away.
travel.railway: Kanchipuram Railway Station, the nearest station (about 3 km from the temple).
travel.road: Well-connected by NH48 from Chennai and Bengaluru; TNSTC and private buses run regularly.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Panguni Uthiram (March-April) for the main festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 am - 12:30 pm and 4:00 pm - 8:30 pm (sources agree; darshan can be crowded during peak hours and festivals).
